description: We’re a team of university students passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems. We’re interested in software development, AI, data, space technology, and creating practical solutions with a strong user experience.
summary: We developed T-MINUS / APOGEX, a browser-based space exploration game with two solo campaigns and a multiplayer expedition for up to 16 players. Crews take specialized roles to assemble spacecraft, complete checks, travel to another planet, recover samples, and bring them home. A server validates multiplayer actions and saves player progress. The project addresses the challenge by making the teamwork and decisions behind a space mission interactive. Players must coordinate engineering, navigation, exploration, and safe return rather than simply watch a mission unfold. We hope the game sparks curiosity about space science and helps players understand how much cooperation a successful mission requires.
details: T-MINUS / APOGEX lets players practice spacecraft assembly and mission operations through solo campaigns, offline play, and a four-team online expedition. Players choose roles, install ship modules, load supplies, run engineering checks, fly, explore, recover samples, and return them for scoring. The game includes mission guidance, accessibility settings, persistent progress, and account recovery. We built it as a browser game using JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Three.js, Node.js, and WebSockets. Playwright and automated tests helped us check gameplay and multiplayer behavior. Our goal is to make space missions engaging while showing the value of planning, technical problem solving, and teamwork.
